newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: UOB beats forecast as net rises 13.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: UOB beats forecast as net rises 13.1 pct.

text.p: Singapore's most profitable bank, United Overseas Bank, beat market forecasts on Thursday with a 13.1 percent rise in net income for 1996 to Singapore $715.5 million (US$496.9 million), up from S$632.7 in 1995.
Chairman and chief executive officer Wee Cho Yaw told reporters the growth came mainly from an 11.3 percent jump in net interest income to S$1.07 billion.
Total group loans and advances grew 15.6 percent to S$27.46 billion by the end of the year.
"I am quite satisfied with these results," Wee said.
Analysts had expected UOB to report a 12 percent rise in net profit to around S$708.8 million.
Wee predicted another batch of double-digit net profit growth figures in a year's time.
"I think our group can continue with double digit profit growth in 1997," he said. "It will be a similar growth."
But Wee said the banking industry was changing and UOB had to move with the times and not rely so much on its traditional sources of income.

"Today in banking we have to be, in my view, not only in lending. Lending is risky and also the margins are very low. We should therefore look more into fee-based and more advisory type of roles," he said.
He said operations such as the management of initial public share offerings showed good prospects for income.
"I think that is where our growth will be focused," he said.
Wee said the bank had to control operational costs if it wanted to meet its target of double-digit net profit growth.
"We need to reduce costs as much as possible and be more efficient," he said.
He said UOB was expanding from its small Singapore domestic market into the Southeast Asia regional market.
Around 32 percent of the bank's after-tax profifs in 1996 came from outside Singapore, from 28 percent in 1995, he said.
"My target is hopefully 40 percent or even 50 percent income from overseas," Wee said.
UOB had already had success in Malaysia where its operations grew 30 percent in 1996, making a net profit of S$131 million.
"The Malaysian economy is still very strong, particularly on the manufacturing side. I still believe Malaysia has a lot of potential and the growth in Malaysia will continue," he said.
He said he expected UOB's Malaysian subsidiaries, Chung Khiaw Bank (Malaysia) Bhd and United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd, to complete their proposed merger by June.
"In principle, Bank Negara has approved our proposal for the banks to merge. It is proceeding. Hopefully by June we will merge as one bank in Malaysia," he said.
The merger would provide cost savings and some other efficiency gains, he said.
-- Singapore newsroom (65 8703199)
